idea-plugin.name: Greppa
idea-plugin.description:
An AI-accelerated coding workflow that understands that some tasks are better done by you. Greppa is built for long-term software projects, where progress depends on your understanding of your own code: AI-assisted coding speeds up prototyping and implementation, but it can also leave you less familiar with what has been written, and keeping the agent, the software and your intent aligned becomes a challenge.

Instead of handing control to an agent that edits the code, Greppa is a soft-assist that follows along as you work: it automatically identifies the tasks you should do yourself, leaves the rest to an agent, analyzes your changes and gives feedback. How agentic it gets is up to you.

An LLM generates a Markdown analysis of the file you are working on, on the fly, and channels it into three workflows in the Greppa tool window:

  • Interpret - understand the code without too much judgement: a clear, informative summary at five levels of difficulty, automatically generated diagrams, explanations focused on the code under your cursor, and explained segments linked to their source lines.
  • Improve - critique the code: compilation and logical errors, immediately explained with a suggested course correction, and tasks sorted into "Critical for understanding" and "Automatable", guided by your own configurable guidelines.
  • Relate - see how the file relates to its dependencies, based on its imports.

Optionally set a topic or goal to focus on; it shapes most or all generated content.

The analysis is fed back to the LLM, enabling auto-complete with an extraordinarily rich context - compilation errors, logical errors, imported code files, your topic or goal, and the code file itself - as well as code action suggestions. For example, auto-complete can finish an import to a library it has already recognized, or a Tetris implementation that uses your graphics.java file.

Greppa works with any OpenAI-compatible provider and bundles its own server, so there is nothing else to install. First-time setup instructions appear in the Greppa tool window.
